body:
My user-level claude.md snippet: 

```
## STAMPED                                                                                                                                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
All projects and datasets should be informed by the  STAMPED principles:                                                                                                                                                      
                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
- **S**elf-contained — everything under one boundary                                                                                                                                                                          
- **T**racked — version control & provenance                                                                                                                                                                                  
- **A**ctionable — executable & documented workflows                                                                                                                                                                          
- **M**odular — independent & composable modules                                                                                                                                                                              
- **P**ortable — runs anywhere with explicit specifications                                                                                                                                                                   
- **E**phemeral — transient compute environment                                                                                                                                                                               
- **D**istributable — shareable, persistent, retrievable                                                                                                                                                                      
                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
When starting a new project, or when specifically asked to apply STAMPED, read the latest version of the paper https://github.com/stamped-principles/stamped-paper/blob/main/main.tex before making suggestions.              
             
```

there is also

- https://github.com/stamped-principles/stamped-skills-assessment
- https://github.com/STAMPED-dl-morphometrics-biases/STAMPED-dl_morphometrics_biases/tree/main/skills

Also prompts were used to directly point to the paper/checklist/etc to guide a particular session to adhere to stamped principles. The example could be 

- https://github.com/dandi/compression-comparisons-t261-study which is the result of running code developed within https://github.com/dandi/compression-comparisons
 
which could account for "lessons" learned from there (check if entire.io is present) which might need to be joined into. 

The idea potentially to develop the ultimate collection of STAMPED skills under umbrella of the https://github.com/con/skills/ and later automate "distribution" with potential "vendorization" (if needed) into this and other (repronim?) repositories.

The idea is to fulfill some specific target use-case(s) while establishing the collection of skills with clearly defined boundaries.

- `/assess-alignment-with-stamped-principles POINTER`
  - verify its alignment to STAMPED principles   
  - Potentially add a stage to review with the user the **goals** of the project and how STAMPED principles could be reflected within the project. Be driven by explicit knowledge from documentation and user, instead of deducing what the project be about when documentation is limited
  - Should not duplicate STAMPED paper/checklist but rather high level summary and prompt to review given current version(s) of those
  - Leave a side-product:  filled out stampled-principles checklist form with the discovered evidence recorded (just as a simple text) for each of the items of the checklist. ATM there is no schema, so should be similar if not identical to what we use internally within checklist web fronend UI and encode within URL e.g. `checklist=0.3.1&responses_version=0.3.1format=3&responses=eyJ...encodedresponses_content...` (research where we have that defined and potentially add a schema for responses within https://github.com/stamped-principles/stamped-checklist-schema .

- `/align-with-stamped-principles PROMPT` -- review existing project and
  - Start with `/assess-alignment-with stamped-principles`   
  - modify or add to potentially existing AI harness (CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md, skills, potentially even spec-kit consitution with subsequent "/speckit.analysis" invocation to setup TODOs etc). The scope and emphasis of what is applied changes depending on the underlying scope and domain of the project. E.g. if it is a dataset, should review it for the aspects of modularity and portability; whenever if it is having a compute component, like transformations, should accent on ephemerality of compute.
  - "align project to STAMPED principles/values" "add STAMPED to it" (keeping it just general and up to `claude code` to decide)  
  - Later potentially propose the skills to be considered such as ours from https://github.com/con/skills/ 
  - So overall keeping it very generic, terse, and offloading a lot upon underlying AI assistant to decide on **how** could be improved.
  - Should inform ***What** to change and **why** it is important to **the project***
  - At the end  redo `/assess-alignment-with stamped-principles` PROMPTing to point to the accomplished or planned out changes and potentially loop back to align more if new obvious work items are not yet planned or some are to be refined or fixed
- `/create-stamped-project PROMPT` which would help to create one given
  - background specific to the use-case given the PROMPT from the user.
  - assess background from the user's environment (e.g. bash history, looking through other AI sessions)
  - potentially grill the user about pointing to projects similar to the target one to get better background and decide on how to structure
  - in all likeness creating an initial structure following the best practices specific to the user and domain
  - delegating to `/align-with-stamped-principles` skill given the PROMPT based on found and sample project projects to point to. 
- `/create-repronim-stamped-project PROMPT` which inside would prepare the prompt for the `/create-stamped-project PROMPT-WITH-REPRONIM-SPECIFICS` (kinda a vendorized invocation, targetting our technologies as e.g. some listed within https://github.com/con/cierge/issues/52)
  - later might be bound somehow with the "repronim-assessment-skill" repronim project is working on, to tune it even more 

For the development of the skills we should define also target to try to prompt and guide subagents to achieve direct use-cases of immediate need to demonstrate:   
- `/do-full-research-loop` naive skill to run the full study. *Make it **ACTIONABLE** as to execute the research project specified in the PROMPT* if initial PROMPT was to carry out the study till the end
- alternative -- give it to "full loop scientist" system to finish it up. 

potential "(de)compositions" later on

- `/self-assess-alignment-with-stamped-principles` -- how given past history and other projects, they are aligned and recommend next steps to improve: ***what** and **why** it is important to you*?

Target use cases
- Some (if not all) of experimentation Ben did in https://zenodo.org/records/19834562
- ReproNim use case(s):
  - "Run X app on openneuro dataset dsXXXXXX subjects X-Y to generate a plot of ZZZ".  "ZZZ" could be as simple as "brain and gray/white matter volume ratios (on secondary axis) vs age"  (could be `ds007116` as was also chosen by @leej3 for his initial attempt; and could be mriqc and plot of overall motion vs age; or just "bet" (brain extraction) with AFNI or whatnot, from some container present within ///repronim/containers; neurodesk must have some.)   Make your agent choose simple one to start with and then progress to more involved
